slides.title: Pineapple on pizza? Let's talk.
slides.sub: Deep breath. This is a safe space.

slides.heading: In Italy, it's a hard no.
paragraphs: Most Italians see pineapple on pizza as a crime against tradition — and they will tell you. Loudly.
Some pizzerias serve it to tourists. Quietly. Without eye contact.

slides.heading: It's not even Italian.
paragraphs: The “Hawaiian” pizza was created in Canada, in 1962, by a Greek-born restaurant owner.
So technically it's a Canadian-Greek-Hawaiian idea. Italy has an alibi.

slides.heading: Sweet fruit, wrong place.
paragraphs: Italian pizza is about balance: tomato, mozzarella and a few great ingredients.
Pineapple's sweetness takes over everything. Like a dinner guest who talks too loud.

slides.heading: Eat what makes you happy.
paragraphs: Just maybe don't order it in Naples. For your own safety.

slides.title: Team pineapple or team Italy?
slides.text: Vote in the comments. Nonna is counting. Follow for Italian Rule Nº 6.

caption:

Pineapple on pizza. Let's talk about it.
